title: What does the XRPL DisallowIncomingCheck account flag mean?
abstract: Sourced explanation of DisallowIncomingCheck and its practical limits.
body:
According to XRPL documentation, DisallowIncomingCheck blocks the creation of incoming Checks for the account under the DisallowIncoming feature. [1]

This controls a specific deferred-payment object, not every possible way of receiving value. It differs from canceling an already existing Check. Review outstanding objects and the target network's supported rules when changing the setting. A sender's ability to make a normal Payment does not prove it may create a Check addressed to the same recipient. [1][2]

XRPL distinguishes an AccountSet option from the AccountRoot bit that records the resulting state. SetFlag and ClearFlag use option identifiers, while the ledger Flags field stores bit values; the numbers are not interchangeable. Read the documented mapping for DisallowIncomingCheck and check the validated account state after any permitted change. A successful submission response alone does not establish that the requested state is final. [1][2]

Author interpretation: document why DisallowIncomingCheck is needed, who may authorize a change and what existing users would experience. Review irreversible settings before issuance and test reversible settings with representative counterparties. This is guidance for interpreting account controls, not a live network measurement. Sources accessed 10 November 2026.
